To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transduction of hRheb with S16H mutation in the substantia of nigra dopaminergic neurons upregulates the levels of both ciliary neurotrophic factors and CNTF receptor alpha and that the hRhebs(S16H)-induced CNTF/CNFTRalpha pathway is protective against 1 methyl 4 phenylpyridinium induced neurotoxicity.
hRheb (S16H) transduction of dopaminergic neuron upregulates CNTF/CNFRα pathway and protects against 1-methy4-phenyl pyridinium-induced neurodegeneration.

transduction of dopaminergic SNpc neurons by AAV-hRheb(S169H) upregulates both CNTF mRNA levels and CNTFRa expression in SNpc dopaminergie neurons and protects them from 1-methyl 4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) neurotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of CNTFRa by hRhebs16H gene delivery.

the activation of the CNTF/Cntfrα signaling pathway by transduction of hRheb (S16H) into dopaminergic neurons, which is neuroprotective against 1-metyl-4-phenylyridinium-induced neurodegeneration in the nigrostratial dopaminergic pathway.
the activation of CNTFR signaling pathway in the substantia Nigra by gene therapy.

activation of Cntf/Cntfrα signaling pathway by hRhebs16h transduction of dopaminergic neuron is a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of PD.

the hRhebs16H gene delivery to dopaminergic neurons upregulates CNTF and its receptor CNTFRA, which in turn is neuroprotective.

hRheb (S16H)-mediated CNTF/CNTRFα signaling pathway may have a neuroprotective potential in the treatment for PD.
activation of Ciliary neurotropic factor (CNTF)/CNTFRα signaling pathway in the nigro-striatal dopaminergic pathway by hRhebs16H may be a useful therapeutic strategy to treat Parkinson’s disease.
